theme: Booking-curve / pace / pickup datasets for hotels and STRs (on-the-books, forward bookings), Key Data / Transparent / Lighthouse (OTA Insight) samples, revenue-management forward curves
queries_run: gh search repos "otb pickup report hotel"
gh search repos "STR RevPAR pace forecast"
gh search repos "hotel occupancy forecast dataset"
gh search repos "look-to-book ratio OR advance booking index"
gh search repos "advance ticket sales OR booked passenger revenue dataset"

candidates.name: revmng
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library for hotel/airline revenue management: single-leg seat/room protection (Littlewood rule, EMSR-a/b, exact dynamic programming), overbooking, pricing, group displacement, length-of-stay controls, network bid prices. No committed booking-pace data, but validated against published worked examples (textbook RM cases) and could be used to build a synthetic OTB/pickup forward-curve model from disclosed occupancy/ADR to sanity-check pace assumptions.
candidates.why_useful: Directly relevant to gap 17 (methods: nowcasting/RM methodology) and to the booking-curve/forward-curve theme even though it carries no proprietary data itself — useful for structuring a pickup model against the ~60%-booked-before-quarter-start framing in CONTEXT.

candidates.name: revmng-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server wrapper around the revmng library exposing the same RM decision functions (seat protection, overbooking, pricing, group/LOS, bid prices, charts) as tools for an AI agent. No data, same author/content as revmng.
candidates.why_useful: Same methodology value as revmng; only worth separate note because it packages the calculators as callable tools, which could be scripted into a pace/pickup sanity-check pipeline.

candidates.name: airdna
candidates.what_it_holds: API Evangelist's independent third-party documentation/profile of the AirDNA Enterprise API surface (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates). It is a written profile of the API's shape, not committed data or a working client with sample pulls; the underlying AirDNA service is paid/subscription.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms what fields a Key-Data/AirDNA-style realised-ADR/occupancy feed would contain (gap 2) if the team later licenses it, but has zero actual data and no free sample export.

candidates.name: airdna-api
candidates.what_it_holds: A client library/wrapper for calling the AirDNA API (paid, key-required) from a property-management company (GuestReady). No committed data, no free sample; requires a paid AirDNA API key which the rules here prohibit using.
candidates.why_useful: Only useful as a reference for what an AirDNA integration looks like; cannot be run under the 'never use paid API keys' rule, and it holds no data itself.

candidates.name: rental-averages
candidates.what_it_holds: Small app that processes exported AirDNA data to compute mean occupancy and ADR averages. It is a post-processing script for a paid AirDNA export, not a data source or free sample itself; no data files committed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: shows the shape of an AirDNA export (occupancy/ADR fields) that would matter for gap 2, but has no data and depends on a paid subscription.

candidates.name: mews-systems
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent profile/documentation of the public API surface for Mews, a cloud PMS/RM platform used by 15,000+ hospitality properties (reservations, distribution, revenue management). Descriptive only; no committed booking-pace or OTB data, and Mews's actual reservation data is per-property/private, not exposed publicly.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal reference for what fields a PMS-level OTB/pickup feed would carry, but there is no accessible aggregate dataset behind it for a public researcher.

candidates.name: hotel_booking_demand_EDA
candidates.what_it_holds: Exploratory data analysis notebook over the well-known Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset (two hotels, ~119k bookings, 2015-2017, lead time and cancellation fields), focused on cancellation-rate trends driven by OTA sales tactics.
candidates.why_useful: This is the same Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset CONTEXT.md already lists as held; flagging only because its lead-time/cancellation-rate framing lines up with gap 3 (booking lead time / cancellation-rate distributions), in case the specific cancellation cut is useful.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) already held per CONTEXT.md

notes: This theme is largely a dead end on GitHub: genuine booking-pace / on-the-books / pickup panels (STR, Key Data Dashboard, Transparent, Lighthouse/OTA Insight, AirDNA Rentalizer) are commercial subscription products with no free sample exports or open mirrors anywhere I could find — every AirDNA-related repo returned by search is either a scraper/client requiring a paid key, a one-off school/portfolio project with zero committed data, or third-party API documentation with no actual data rows. Searches for 'hotel booking pace', 'otb pickup report hotel', 'STR RevPAR pace forecast', 'hotel occupancy forecast dataset', 'look-to-book ratio OR advance booking index', and 'advance ticket sales OR booked passenger revenue dataset' (as an NCLH-style book-ahead analogue) all returned zero or irrelevant hits (mostly Power BI dashboard projects with no data files, or generic ML boilerplate on the already-held Portugal hotel-booking-demand Kaggle dataset). The only genuinely reusable finds are two revenue-management CALCULATION libraries (arikanatakan/revmng and its MCP wrapper) that implement textbook RM forward-curve/protection-level math (Littlewood, EMSR, DP) validated against published worked examples — useful as methodology, not data. Recommend: if this theme is re-scouted, try WebSearch (not gh) for 'Key Data Dashboard sample export', 'OTA Insight Lighthouse benchmark report pdf', or academic RM papers with replication code on Zenodo/OSF rather than GitHub search, since the vendors in question do not open-source samples. GitHub search API rate-limited once mid-run (HTTP 403); recovered after ~40s wait. Also hit the session's WebSearch budget cap (200/200) partway through, so no WebSearch cross-checks were possible for this pass — worth a follow-up scout with WebSearch quota specifically for Key Data / Transparent / Lighthouse sample data, which is unlikely to live on GitHub at all.
